executableExamples.rationale: Link-only corrections do not change executable content. Existing snippets were read and preservation checked, not recompiled or run against a database.

baseline: The original extensionless Jakarta URL returned HTTP 404; both owned references are corrected.

walkthroughs: Case A: product authority defines uniqueness within tenant and method. One table per method with UNIQUE(tenant_id, provider_reference) satisfies the shown scope; IDs 101 and 102 are distinct. Retaining the existing mapping is appropriate without other evidence of a defect.

Case B: the identical two rows violate cross-method uniqueness. The shared primary-key sequence is unrelated to that business-key constraint. A common constrained table or a transactionally maintained shared-key registry is a candidate; all writers and historical conflicts must be handled before a rollout can be called safe.
behavioralEvaluations.technicalExecutionDistinction: Only package validation, URL retrieval and fixture integrity were executed. Neither walkthrough is an agent output, provider integration result or database concurrency test.

cases.decisiveConstraint: Only providerReferenceUniqueWithin in business-contract.json differs. All schema, mapping, query, history and sample-row artifacts are identical.
cases.expectedDifference: Preserve valid method-scoped uniqueness in A; recognize the missing cross-method enforcement in B without mandating a universal mapping strategy.
cases.prerequisites: Read-only fixture review; Java 17, Hibernate ORM 6.6 mapping inventory, PostgreSQL 18 DDL. No runnable ORM project or database is provided.
cases.isolation: Coordinator must provide one case and intended skill treatment. Evaluator-only criteria, paired answer, handoff and prior results are excluded. Folder separation alone is not enforced isolation.

sources.support: Correct versioned destination for both broken links. Existing hierarchy identity, optional TABLE_PER_CLASS portability, discriminator defaults and bulk-DML state/version caveats agree with the specification.
Confirms provider-specific UNION behavior and inclusion of concrete entity tables in polymorphic queries. It does not establish performance for an application or portability to other providers.

Confirms the existing qualification that external database changes are not automatically visible to provider caches; a fresh persistence context alone is insufficient evidence of migration consistency.
Supports existing database/version-specific cautions about validation and locking. No actual migration or lock-duration measurement was performed.
Grounds the case review of table-local uniqueness: a UNIQUE on each leaf table does not enforce a business key across the two separate tables.
Confirms conditional index selection is database-specific and predicate-sensitive, consistent with the existing qualified guidance. No query-plan claim was made.

assumptions: The existing skill remains a review/design aid; this assignment does not implement or deploy a persistence strategy.
Cases are bounded synthetic project artifacts, not evidence of any real application workload.
limits: The correction restores source accessibility; it does not establish incremental agent behavior improvement.
No ORM bootstrapping, SQL execution, migration, raw-SQL hostile fixture, concurrent write, query plan, cache integration or performance benchmark was executed.
A shared primary-key sequence in the synthetic inputs does not prove arbitrary writers obey an identity policy; real all-writer enforcement still needs review.
Source inspection supports static contracts only; real mapping overrides, database version/collation, provider SQL, constraints, writer coverage and rollout behavior require application evidence.
The Hibernate 6.6 guide is a moving maintenance-series URL; observed patch 6.6.58.Final is recorded, not assumed to be every consumer runtime.
The local loader used existing compiled repository modules without rebuilding. Catalog-wide routing, generated integrity/version data and full verification remain coordinator-owned.
